name: RedStore
tagline: Lightweight C RDF triplestore with a built-in SPARQL HTTP server, built on the Redland libraries.
description: RedStore is a small RDF triplestore written in C by Nicholas Humfrey on top of the Redland RDF libraries (raptor, rasqal and librdf). It bundles its own HTTP server exposing a SPARQL 1.0 query endpoint plus the SPARQL 1.1 Protocol, Graph Store HTTP Protocol and Service Description, so you can load, replace and delete named graphs with curl. Storage is delegated to any context-capable Redland backend, including in-memory hashes, SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL and Virtuoso, and there was a packaged Mac OS X app. It was handy for local Linked Data development, but the last release was 0.5.4 in 2011, the last commit in 2017, and it only advertises SPARQL 1.0 query support.
statusNote: Last release 0.5.4 (2011), last commit 2017; unmaintained. Use Oxigraph, Apache Jena Fuseki or QLever.

scale.notes: Capacity depends on the chosen Redland storage backend; intended for small and medium graphs.

strengths: Tiny footprint with only the Redland libraries as a runtime dependency
Built-in HTTP server with Graph Store Protocol for curl-friendly graph loading
Pluggable storage via Redland backends (hashes, SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Virtuoso)
Reads and writes many RDF serialisations
weaknesses: Unmaintained since 2017; only SPARQL 1.0 query is advertised, with no SPARQL 1.1 Update
Performance bounded by Redland storage modules
useCases: Local Linked Data experiments and teaching
Lightweight SPARQL endpoint for small legacy datasets
